rejected.title: Types of efficiency
card: Allocative
Resources go to making the goods and services that people value most. Output matches what society wants.
Productive
Goods are made using the fewest resources, so the cost of each unit is as low as it can be.
Dynamic
The economy adapts to change over time, such as new technology or changing tastes, by shifting what it makes and how it makes it.
Intertemporal
Resources are balanced between the present and the future. Using more now, such as for spending, can mean less later.
rejected.remember: Efficiency can mean the right goods, the lowest cost, change over time, or balance between now and later.

a.q: A bakery in Ballarat makes the same number of loaves as last year, but each loaf now uses less flour and power. Which type of efficiency does this lower resource use per loaf show?
opts: Productive efficiency
Allocative efficiency
Dynamic efficiency
Intertemporal efficiency
a.why: Productive efficiency means making goods with the fewest resources, and using less flour and power for each loaf is exactly that. Dynamic efficiency is about adapting to change, such as new tastes or technology, but the question asks only about resources used per loaf.
a.clue: Look at the resources used for each loaf.

b.q: A council in Victoria spends all its budget on new sports fields now and sets aside nothing for repairs in future years. Which efficiency does this most directly concern?
opts: Intertemporal efficiency, as it trades later for now
Productive efficiency, as it lifts the cost of each field
Allocative efficiency, as people may not want fields
Dynamic efficiency, as fields cannot adapt to change
b.why: The choice is about using resources now at the cost of later years, which is intertemporal efficiency. Allocative efficiency would need evidence about what people value, and nothing here shows a higher cost per field.
b.clue: Which type weighs the present against the future?

draft.title: Types of efficiency
card: Allocative
Resources go to making the goods and services that people value most. Output matches what society wants.
Productive
Goods are made using the fewest resources, so the cost of each unit is as low as it can be.
Dynamic
The economy adapts and improves over time, through new technology, new methods and changing tastes.
Intertemporal
Resources are shared between the present and the future. Using more now, such as for spending, can mean less later.
draft.remember: Efficiency can mean the right goods, the lowest cost, change over time, or balance between now and later.

a.q: A bakery in Ballarat changes its ovens and layout so it bakes the same bread using less flour and power. Which efficiency has improved?
opts: Productive efficiency
Allocative efficiency
Dynamic efficiency
Intertemporal efficiency
a.why: The same output now uses fewer resources, which is productive efficiency. Allocative efficiency would be about whether bread is what people value most. Dynamic efficiency is about change over time, not one cost saving.
a.clue: Look at the resources used for the same bread.

b.q: A council in Victoria spends all its budget on new sports fields now and sets aside nothing for repairs in future years. Which efficiency does this most directly concern?
opts: Intertemporal efficiency, as it trades later for now
Productive efficiency, as it lifts the cost of each field
Allocative efficiency, as people may not want fields
Dynamic efficiency, as fields cannot adapt to change
b.why: The choice is about using resources now at the cost of later years, which is intertemporal efficiency. Allocative efficiency would need evidence about what people value. Nothing here shows higher cost per unit.
b.clue: Which type weighs the present against the future?

b.best: Intertemporal efficiency, as it trades later for now

problems.detail: The bakery 'changes its ovens and layout', which is new technology and new methods. The card lists exactly these under dynamic efficiency, so a student could defend 'Dynamic efficiency'. Describe a change that only cuts waste with no new technology or method, or ask which efficiency is shown by the lower resource use per loaf.

The why says dynamic efficiency is 'not one cost saving', but the card defines dynamic efficiency as improving through new technology and methods. That fits a firm adopting new ovens, so the why rests on a distinction the card never teaches.

check.summary: Question a's bakery adopts new ovens and a new layout, so 'Dynamic efficiency' is defensible from the card's own definition. The why dismisses it on a distinction the card does not make. Question b is fine.
